source.title: A Tale Of Two Long Tails
source.authors: Daniel D'Souza; Zach Nussbaum; Chirag Agarwal; Sara Hooker

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains on datasets with known noisy and atypical subsets and tracks their learning dynamics using MSP ranks. This conceptually tests whether noisy and non-noisy examples are learned differently over training, but it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for datasets containing 20% noisy labels, but does not vary the corruption fraction or report training error on a fully randomly labeled dataset. Those accuracy results are recorded under fits_no_version. The plotted MSP rankings are reported in prose for the augmentation conditions and are rows for V6. References to Arpit et al. are prior work, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study measures uncertainty-score rankings and test accuracy, not fitting or memorization rates. Its MSP-rank trajectories cannot establish whether shared real-data patterns are fitted before noisy labels. Under the stated exclusion for confidence-score measures, these results do not test V6 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that standard and targeted augmentation amplify differences between atypical and noisy uncertainty-score distributions, with targeted augmentation providing the strongest separation. They interpret late noisy-score increases under standard augmentation as memorization and suggest targeted augmentation may better prevent it. The record's statement that learning rate helps distinguish uncertainty sources is unsupported; the conclusion concerns learning dynamics under added information.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains WideResNet on datasets containing 20% noisy, 20% atypical, and 60% typical examples and tracks subset MSP ranks under augmentation variants; it does not reproduce the original fully random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The MSP-rank separation varies with augmentation: no augmentation yields overlap, standard augmentation separates the groups with some late overlap, and targeted augmentation preserves separation.

fits_no_version.finding: Without augmentation, atypical and noisy MSP-rank distributions increasingly overlap during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uncertainty rankings alone fail to distinguish atypical from mislabeled training examples in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard augmentation separates atypical and noisy uncertainty ranks, with some late overlap; targeted augmentation maintains separation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Augmentation protocols can improve uncertainty-based separation of atypical and mislabeled examples, with targeted augmentation providing the clearest separation.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 20% noisy-subset fraction, targeted augmentation gives the highest reported CIFAR-10 test accuracy, while standard augmentation gives the highest CIFAR-100 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of targeted versus standard augmentation depends on the dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: Presented at the ICML 2021 Workshop on Uncertainty and Robustness in Deep Learning.
record.problems: The paper does not report training error for the noisy subset or directly measure memorization; its dynamics evidence is qualitative MSP-rank plots described in text. It uses a fixed 20% noisy fraction and does not test the claim's corruption-fraction sweep.

untested.parts: No fully random-label training experiment, near-zero training-error result, or associated chance-level test-error result.
No comparison of convergence times for real and random labels or corruption-dependent convergence.
No fitting experiments on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
No corruption-fraction sweep or joint measurement of perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance.
No measurement of random-label fitting under regularization or of the effects of removing regularization on clean-label generalization.
No direct measurement of shared-pattern fitting before noisy-label memorization; only relative uncertainty-score trajectories are reported.

record.verdict_notes: MSP here is the softmax probability assigned to the training label, rather than necessarily the maximum predicted probability. Relative ranks provide neither training-error rates nor proof of memorization. The paper reports no learning-rate ablation, and none of its results establishes that random-label fitting is prevented.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not train on a completely randomly labeled training set or report its training error and test error at chance.
The study does not compare time to convergence for true and random labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
The study does not train on shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study uses a fixed 20% noisy subset; it does not sweep corruption from none to all or report test error rising toward chance.
The study does not test whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether removing them impairs generalization on true labels.

The study tracks MSP ranks for atypical and noisy subsets in datasets with 20% noisy labels. It does not compare a fully true-labeled dataset with a fully randomly labeled one, nor measure training error directly.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked MSP ranks of atypical and noisy examples across training without augmentation.
rows.measure: Distribution of MSP ranks for atypical and noisy subsets across training; the distributions overlap, increasingly so over training.
rows.value: Atypical and noisy examples are accorded the same range of low probabilities; by the end of training their sources cannot be distinguished using probabilistic ranking.
rows.note: The paper describes the plotted result qualitatively.
rows.check: Overlapping uncertainty ranks do not establish absent real-label-first learning.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Tracked MSP ranks of atypical and noisy examples across training with standard augmentation.
rows.measure: Distribution of MSP ranks for atypical and noisy subsets across training.
rows.value: Atypical MSP ranks rise more markedly while noisy MSP ranks remain at the bottom; toward the end, noisy MSP scores begin to rise steadily, causing a small degree of overlap.
rows.note: The authors attribute the late rise to propensity for memorization of noisy examples.
rows.check: Atypical ranks rising before noisy scores is a confidence-proxy result; the authors' memorization explanation is an attribution, not a direct measurement.
